title: What Happens When You Delete a File?
sources: Wikipedia, 'Trim (computing)': the OS tells the SSD which blocks are no longer in use so it can erase them; after TRIM, deleted data is usually unrecoverable
ScienceABC, 'Where do deleted files go?': deleting removes the file system's pointer/entry and marks the space as available; the bytes stay until overwritten
PITS Data Recovery, 'Where Do Deleted Files Go': emptied Recycle Bin files can often be recovered from hard drives until new data overwrites them
Rossmann Group, 'SSD TRIM / garbage collection': on TRIM-enabled SSDs, deleted blocks are cleared by garbage collection and many drives return zeros for trimmed blocks right away

lines.text: You delete a photo and empty the trash,
so it's gone for good, right?
Your drive keeps a kind of table of contents
that says where every file lives.
Deleting just removes the file's entry from that list
and marks its space as free to reuse.
But the actual data is still sitting there,
which is why recovery apps can bring it back.
once new files get saved on top,
the old data is overwritten, and then it's really gone.
And on modern SSDs, that cleanup can happen almost right away.
lines.caps: AND ON *MODERN | *SSDS | THAT *CLEANUP | CAN *HAPPEN | ALMOST *RIGHT AWAY

lines.text: So deleting doesn't erase a file, it just forgets where it was.
lines.caps: SO *DELETING | DOESN'T *ERASE | A *FILE | IT JUST *FORGETS | WHERE IT *WAS
